sources.citation: Evans, Nicholas. 1990. The Minkin language of the Burketown region. In G.N. O'Grady & D.T. Tryon (eds), Studies in comparative Pama-Nyungan, 173-207. Pacific Linguistics C-111. Canberra: ANU. DOI 10.15144/PL-C111.173 (CC BY-SA online edition via sealang/CRCL).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Phonology section (pp.178-181) reconstructs a tentative phoneme inventory (retroflexes, palatals, interdentals, rhotics) and phonotactics from three 19th-century wordlists; Evans states 'the Minkin corpus is too unreliable and too restricted for definite conclusions.. All statements about Minkin phonology must therefore be tentative in the extreme' (p.178). No mention of stress or accent anywhere in the chapter (a full-text search for stress/accent + page reads).

sources.citation: Curr, Edward M. 1886. The Australian Race, vol. II. Melbourne: John Ferres. List No. 90 'Burketown' by Thomas Coward (pp.298-299) and No. 94 'On the west bank of the Leichhardt River, near the sea - Mingin tribe' by E. Curr (p.314ff). archive.org scanned (cu31924026093827).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; bare English-Minkin wordlists with short introductions, no accent marks or prosodic remarks.
